chunks: Then bring your scripture, if what you say is true.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Then bring your scripture, if what you say is true'?
ai.summary: In Surah As-Saff, this verse serves as a divine challenge (istidraj) to polytheists and Jews, demanding they produce a scripture equal to the Quran if they claim it is not from God. Shia exegetes, such as Al-Tabarsi, highlight this as a rhetorical device exposing the insufficiency of their own traditions compared to the final, preserved revelation. It underscores the concept of Tawatur and the Quran's unique status as the ultimate criterion (Furqan) against fabricated claims.
